II. Kernel Structures — Reverse Word Search (place these words)
EXOKERNEL — minimalist kernel that exposes hardware to applications, giving them direct control.
HYBRID KERNEL — combines features of monolithic and microkernels; used in Windows and macOS.
LAYERED — organized in levels; each layer builds on services provided by the one below it.
MICROKERNEL — only essential functions like IPC and basic scheduling; everything else in user space.
MODULAR — components can be loaded and unloaded at runtime; used in Linux systems (LKMs).
MONOLITHIC — single large process running entirely in kernel mode with all OS services included.
SIMPLE — basic structure with minimal functionality, used in teaching or early systems (e.g. MS-DOS).
VIRTUAL MACHINE (HYPERVISOR) — abstracts physical hardware; runs multiple OSes on the same system.
